searches.description: Identify ortholog groups based on the median percent identity of all protein sequences within each group. Median percent identity serves as an indicator of group cohesiveness: higher values suggest a tightly clustered group with minimal outliers, while lower values indicate a more dispersed group. Percent identity is represented in decimal form and ranges from 0 to 1 (the equivalent of 0% to 100%). For example, setting the percent identity threshold between 0.8 and 1 will return ortholog groups with a median percent identity between 80% and 100%.

searches.description:
Find Ortholog Groups by phyletic pattern.

Phyletic Pattern Expression is a flexible and powerful way to identify ortholog groups with a certain conservation pattern. The pattern is used to identify groups based on whether proteins from specific taxa are present or absent. Also, the pattern finds groups with a certain copy number (e.g., duplications) within specified taxa.

Examples

These expressions find ortholog groups in which...
hsap>=5there are five or more human sequences
hsap+ecol=2Tboth human and E. coli are present.
hsap+ecol=1Tonly one species of human or E. coli is present.
hsap+ecol>=1Tonly one or both species of human and E. coli is present.
hsap+ecol>=10there are 10 or more human or E. Coli sequences.
EUKA=5there are exactly eukaryotic 5 sequences
EUKA=5Tthere are exactly eukaryotic 5 taxa
hsap+FIRM=2Tthere are exactly 2 human or Gram-positive bacteria taxa
EUKA=35Tthere are all 35 eukaryotic species, ie, Eukaryota-universal groups
EUKA>=5T AND hsap>=10there are at least five eukaryotic species and containing at least 10 human sequences.
(EUKA>=5T AND hsap>=10) OR pfal<20there are at least five eukaryotic species and containing at least 10 human sequences, or there are less than 20 P. falciparum sequences.
ALL=564Tthere are 564 OrthoMCL species. (click on ALL in the graphical display to get up-to-date total number.

Tips

  • Avoid redundancy in your PPE. For example, hsap>=1 is equal to hsap=1T, so no need to mention them twice.
  • Merge different PPE units for faster execution. For example hsap=1T AND mmus=1T can be merged as hsap+mmus=2T.

The PPE Grammar in Detail

Individual grammatical units of PPE expressions are composed of two parts:

  1. A taxa specification. This can be any one of:
    • a species abbreviation (e.g. tgon)
    • a clade abbreviation (e.g., BACT for all Eubacteria taxa)
    • a list of species or clade abbreviations linked by plus sign "+" (e.g. tgon+pfal+hsap+FIRM).
    • ALL to represent all taxa in OrthoMCL.
  2. A logical comparison operator followed by a count.
    • operators allowed are: >, <, =, >=, and <=
    • the count is either:
      • a number, such as 5. This is a count of sequences that the operator applies to.
      • a number with a T, such as 5T. This is a count of taxa that the operator applies to.

Multiple expression units may be combined using AND or OR, and may use parentheses to provide explicit execution ordering.

searches.description:
Find Proteins that contain a motif pattern that you specify., e.g. "CC6+RK", which means "two cysteines followed by one or more hydrophobic amino acids, followed by arginine, then lysine". The pattern need not be well conserved. If you can describe it in words, you can probably use this tool to create an "expression" that can search other proteins for similar patterns.

Another example is the pattern of the Pexel motif, which can be represented as "R.L.[EQD]", meaning "an arginine, then any amino acid, then a leucine, then any amino acid, then either an aspartic acid, a glutamic acid, or a glutamine".

Specify the pattern with a (Perl style) "regular expression". (Regular expressions are more powerful than PROSITE patterns.) For a description of how to create regular expressions, please see the Regular Expression Tutorial.

The following codes can be used to represent classes of amino acids.
AA property Amino acids Code
Acidic DE 0
Alcohol ST 1
Aliphatic ILV 2
Aromatic FHWY 3
Basic KRH 4
Charged DEHKR 5
Hydrophobic AVILMFYW 6
Hydrophilic KRHDENQ 7
Polar CDEHKNQRST 8
Small ACDGNPSTV 9
Tiny AGS B
Turnlike ACDEGHKNQRST Z
Any ACDEFGHIKLM
NPQRSTVWY 		.

group.description: Identify ortholog groups based on the median percent identity of all protein sequences within each group. Median percent identity serves as an indicator of group cohesiveness: higher values suggest a tightly clustered group with minimal outliers, while lower values indicate a more dispersed group. Percent identity is represented in decimal form and ranges from 0 to 1 (the equivalent of 0% to 100%). For example, setting the percent identity threshold between 0.8 and 1 will return ortholog groups with a median percent identity between 80% and 100%.

group.description:
Find Ortholog Groups by phyletic pattern.

Phyletic Pattern Expression is a flexible and powerful way to identify ortholog groups with a certain conservation pattern. The pattern is used to identify groups based on whether proteins from specific taxa are present or absent. Also, the pattern finds groups with a certain copy number (e.g., duplications) within specified taxa.

Examples

These expressions find ortholog groups in which...
hsap>=5there are five or more human sequences
hsap+ecol=2Tboth human and E. coli are present.
hsap+ecol=1Tonly one species of human or E. coli is present.
hsap+ecol>=1Tonly one or both species of human and E. coli is present.
hsap+ecol>=10there are 10 or more human or E. Coli sequences.
EUKA=5there are exactly eukaryotic 5 sequences
EUKA=5Tthere are exactly eukaryotic 5 taxa
hsap+FIRM=2Tthere are exactly 2 human or Gram-positive bacteria taxa
EUKA=35Tthere are all 35 eukaryotic species, ie, Eukaryota-universal groups
EUKA>=5T AND hsap>=10there are at least five eukaryotic species and containing at least 10 human sequences.
(EUKA>=5T AND hsap>=10) OR pfal<20there are at least five eukaryotic species and containing at least 10 human sequences, or there are less than 20 P. falciparum sequences.
ALL=564Tthere are 564 OrthoMCL species. (click on ALL in the graphical display to get up-to-date total number.

Tips

  • Avoid redundancy in your PPE. For example, hsap>=1 is equal to hsap=1T, so no need to mention them twice.
  • Merge different PPE units for faster execution. For example hsap=1T AND mmus=1T can be merged as hsap+mmus=2T.

The PPE Grammar in Detail

Individual grammatical units of PPE expressions are composed of two parts:

  1. A taxa specification. This can be any one of:
    • a species abbreviation (e.g. tgon)
    • a clade abbreviation (e.g., BACT for all Eubacteria taxa)
    • a list of species or clade abbreviations linked by plus sign "+" (e.g. tgon+pfal+hsap+FIRM).
    • ALL to represent all taxa in OrthoMCL.
  2. A logical comparison operator followed by a count.
    • operators allowed are: >, <, =, >=, and <=
    • the count is either:
      • a number, such as 5. This is a count of sequences that the operator applies to.
      • a number with a T, such as 5T. This is a count of taxa that the operator applies to.

Multiple expression units may be combined using AND or OR, and may use parentheses to provide explicit execution ordering.

sequence.description:
This tool will map a set of proteins (usually a complete proteome from an organism)
            to OrthoMCL groups using Diamond blastp. Query proteins with no significant match to
            any OrthoMCL proteins will be shown in the results list with an asterisk (*) for the
            matched protein and an e-value of -1. The search could take from a few minutes to a
            few hours depending on the size of your input file and the load on our servers.

sequence.description:
Find Proteins that contain a motif pattern that you specify., e.g. "CC6+RK", which means "two cysteines followed by one or more hydrophobic amino acids, followed by arginine, then lysine". The pattern need not be well conserved. If you can describe it in words, you can probably use this tool to create an "expression" that can search other proteins for similar patterns.

Another example is the pattern of the Pexel motif, which can be represented as "R.L.[EQD]", meaning "an arginine, then any amino acid, then a leucine, then any amino acid, then either an aspartic acid, a glutamic acid, or a glutamine".

Specify the pattern with a (Perl style) "regular expression". (Regular expressions are more powerful than PROSITE patterns.) For a description of how to create regular expressions, please see the Regular Expression Tutorial.

The following codes can be used to represent classes of amino acids.
AA property Amino acids Code
Acidic DE 0
Alcohol ST 1
Aliphatic ILV 2
Aromatic FHWY 3
Basic KRH 4
Charged DEHKR 5
Hydrophobic AVILMFYW 6
Hydrophilic KRHDENQ 7
Polar CDEHKNQRST 8
Small ACDGNPSTV 9
Tiny AGS B
Turnlike ACDEGHKNQRST Z
Any ACDEFGHIKLM
NPQRSTVWY 		.
